In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best measure depends on the task at hand.
the context vector method is the best for semantic relatedness and the path-based measures are the best for semantic similarity.
the path-based measures, the information content measure, and the context vector measure all provide useful measures of semantic relatedness for the medical domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need to develop a measure that can capture both the similarity and the relatedness of biomedical concepts.
the context vector and information content measures are better for capturing the physicians' ratings, and the path-based measures better for capturing the medical coders' ratings.
we have shown how to adapt existing measures of semantic similarity to SNOMED- CT and how these measures can be evaluated in a biomedical context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
measures of similarity and relatedness are not universal.
the choice of measure is highly dependent on the task at hand, and that there is no one-size-fits-all approach to semantic similarity.
measures that combine both information from ontological structures and information from corpora are likely to provide the most accurate results.
